StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

InstanceType.maps_to: no sim counterpart; cmds.py:308 keys stacking on power id alone
InstanceType.issue: PowerInstanceType.Instanced (RollingBoulderPower.cs:24) means every application is an independently tracked instance with its own growing Amount; the sim's PowerCmd.apply merges by id via on_stack (cmds.py:308-311). This is audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json's gap G5 and is not re-verdicted here (binding rule 3) -- G5 lists this power as one of its 11 ported InstanceType units and notes it is among the nine that do not acknowledge the distinction at all, unlike ToricToughnessPower and TheBombPower. What is PER-UNIT is reachability, and for this power two simultaneous instances are REACHABLE and the divergence is arithmetic, not just bookkeeping: the ported Colorless card Rolling Boulder (cards/colorless_powers.py:294-314) is a normal deck card that can be drawn and played twice in one combat, and it applies 5 each time. Two C# instances then deal 5 + 5 = 10 on the next turn and 10 + 10 = 20 on the one after (each grows by its own +5, RollingBoulderPower.cs:52); one merged sim instance holds 10 and deals 10, then 15, then 20 -- so the sim is 5 short on turn 2 and 5 short again on turn 3, converging only later. It also fires ONE damage sweep where the game fires two, which halves the number of on_damage_received dispatches (Thorns, Curl Up) the enemies see. This is the clearest reachable G5 witness among the ported InstanceType units and is recorded here for the seam session's dormancy argument. RULE-3 NOTE (2026-07-26 review fix pass): power/the_bomb, the other ported G5 unit that hand-rolls a workaround, carried `deliberate-divergence` on this same mechanism and is now `gap` too, so G5 has one verdict at every site. Its residue is state-shaped rather than arithmetic -- one merged power at `amount = min(fuses)` where the game has N instances with N Amounts -- because its fuse list does reproduce the damage exactly.

AfterPlayerTurnStart.issue: Post-draw on both sides (CombatManager.cs:675 vs player.py:186), so the slot itself is right. The gap is the phase collapse: PHASE COLLAPSE. The sim's on_player_turn_started (player.py:186) is a single slot serving THREE distinct C# phases that the game runs in a fixed order: Hook.AfterPlayerTurnStart (CombatManager.cs:675, inside the SetupPlayerTurn task launched at :514), then Hook.AfterSideTurnStart (:522), then Hook.AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered (:568 -> RunAutoPrePlayPhase, :613-619). Collapsing them makes the relative order of this power and every other turn-start power a function of hook-REGISTRATION order, i.e. of which card the player happened to play first. Same shape as hook_dispatch's G3 (the Early/Late phase passes do not exist) one level up, and the AutoPrePlay/AutoPostPlay half of it is turn_structure's G8; neither is re-verdicted here per binding rule 3, but see this record's Mayhem guard for the executed consequence.

guards.issue: The sim iterates combat.enemies filtered on not enemy.is_gone (powers.py:3716) where C# uses CombatState.HittableEnemies, which additionally consults Hook.ShouldAllowHitting (Creature.cs:308-322), so the sim aims at creatures the game considers unhittable -- a mid-revival Illusion (powers.py:1572-1575) or a withered Decimillipede segment (powers.py:2354-2357). DORMANT: DamageCmd.deal re-checks should_allow_hitting at entry (cmds.py:51-52) and returns 0, so no damage lands; what still differs is that the command runs at all. Same finding and same verdict as power/inferno's and power/constrict's HittableEnemies guards, per binding rule 3. NOTE the non-TestMode arm (RollingBoulderPower.cs:39-51) fires the damage tasks per creature off a targeting SIGNAL and awaits them together; that is presentation/targeting plumbing and the TestMode arm is the canonical semantics. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: powers.py:3717-3720 passes DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (valueprops.py:42 -- UNPOWERED alone, so blockable, matching C# omitting Unblockable) and dealer=self.owner. Both the props and the dealer are right, which is worth recording: this is the same call shape whose omitted props made power/feel_no_pain and power/curl_up live gaps, and the same dealer= that power/thorns and power/constrict drop.

The increment is 5 on both sides: RollingBoulderPower.cs:26's CanonicalVars declares new DamageVar(5m, ValueProp.Unpowered) and powers.py:3706 sets INCREMENT = 5. Non-ascension by construction (no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file). The sim also fires hooks.on_power_amount_changed for the growth (powers.py:3724), which C# gets from SetAmount's own notification path. Third-file citation, not hashed here.

guards.what: The sim ADDS an end-of-combat check the C# power does not have
guards.rationale: powers.py:3721-3722 calls combat._end_combat(player_won=True) when the boulder killed the last enemy, and :3714 bails when combat.is_over. C# has neither -- the win check is CombatManager's job (CheckWinCondition), and Hook.IterateCombatHookListeners' IsOverOrEnding gate (Hook.cs:53-63) is what stops later listeners, which is hook_dispatch's G8. The sim needs the inline call because it has no such gate. Same observable (the combat ends and the player wins), different mechanism, and it is the sim compensating for a recorded engine gap rather than a divergence of this power.

guards.what: Registration-order contention with Mayhem in the collapsed slot
guards.issue: LIVE, and it widens turn_structure's G8. MayhemPower is C#'s third ported AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered implementer (MayhemPower.cs, applied by the ported Colorless power card Mayhem -- cards/colorless_powers.py:157-174) and G8 does not name it: G8 calls its AutoPrePlay half DORMANT on the grounds that 'the two ported users' effects (play cards / auto-play one Skill) do not read any other turn-start listener's output', naming only Whispering Earring and the Imbued enchantment. Mayhem does read another turn-start listener's output, and the pair is executed below. In the game Mayhem's auto-plays run at CombatManager.cs:568, strictly AFTER Hook.AfterSideTurnStart (:522) and after SetupPlayerTurn's Hook.AfterPlayerTurnStart (:675); in the sim MayhemPower.on_player_turn_started (powers.py:3572-3583) sits in the same dispatch as this power, so the order is registration order. EXECUTED with RollingBoulderPower 5 + MayhemPower 1 against a 4-HP enemy and one Strike on top of the draw pile: applying the boulder FIRST kills the enemy, ends the combat, and Mayhem's own combat.is_over guard (powers.py:3577) then leaves the Strike in the DRAW pile; applying Mayhem first plays the Strike into the DISCARD pile and the boulder fires after. The game always resolves the boulder first, so the Strike is never played. The final pile of a card is conformance-visible and is in the RL observation, and an extra play perturbs every later shuffle. Both cards are ported Colorless power cards (cards/colorless_powers.py:294-314 and :157-174).
